markers.details:

or annotation "cert-manager.io/inject-ca-from-secret" for a CRD that needs CA injection.

fields.name: annotations

fields.name: labels

markers.name: kubebuilder:printcolumn
markers.summary: adds a column to "kubectl get" output for this CRD.

fields.name: JSONPath
fields.summary: specifies the jsonpath expression used to extract the value of the column.

fields.name: description

fields.name: format

fields.details:
It may be any OpenAPI data format corresponding to the type, listed at

fields.name: name

fields.name: priority

fields.details:
Lower priority (*higher* numbered) columns will be hidden if the terminal
width is too small.

fields.name: type

fields.details:

markers.name: kubebuilder:resource
markers.summary: configures naming and scope for a CRD.

fields.name: categories
fields.summary: specifies which group aliases this resource is part of.
fields.details:
Group aliases are used to work with groups of resources at once.
The most common one is "all" which covers about a third of the base
resources in Kubernetes, and is generally used for "user-facing" resources.

fields.name: path
fields.summary: specifies the plural "resource" for this CRD.
fields.details:
It generally corresponds to a plural, lower-cased version of the Kind.
See https://book.kubebuilder.io/cronjob-tutorial/gvks.html.

fields.name: scope
fields.summary: overrides the scope of the CRD (Cluster vs Namespaced).
fields.details:
Scope defaults to "Namespaced".  Cluster-scoped ("Cluster") resources
don't exist in namespaces.

fields.name: shortName
fields.summary: specifies aliases for this CRD.
fields.details:
Short names are often used when people have work with your resource
over and over again.  For instance, "rs" for "replicaset" or
"crd" for customresourcedefinition.

fields.name: singular
fields.summary: overrides the singular form of your resource.
fields.details: The singular form is otherwise defaulted off the plural (path).

markers.name: kubebuilder:selectablefield
markers.summary: adds a field that may be used with field selectors.

fields.name: JSONPath
fields.summary: specifies the jsonpath expression which is used to produce a field selector value.

markers.name: kubebuilder:skip
markers.summary: don't consider this package as an API version.

markers.name: kubebuilder:skipversion
markers.summary: removes the particular version of the CRD from the CRDs spec.
markers.details:
This is useful if you need to skip generating and listing version entries
for 'internal' resource versions, which typically exist if using the
Kubernetes upstream conversion-gen tool.

markers.name: kubebuilder:storageversion
markers.summary: marks this version as the "storage version" for the CRD for conversion.
markers.details:
When conversion is enabled for a CRD (i.e. it's not a trivial-versions/single-version CRD),
one version is set as the "storage version" to be stored in etcd.  Attempting to store any
other version will result in conversion to the storage version via a conversion webhook.

markers.name: kubebuilder:subresource:scale
markers.summary: enables the "/scale" subresource on a CRD.

fields.name: selectorpath
fields.summary: specifies the jsonpath to the pod label selector field for the scale's status.
fields.details:
The selector field must be the *string* form (serialized form) of a selector.
Setting a pod label selector is necessary for your type to work with the HorizontalPodAutoscaler.

fields.name: specpath
fields.summary: specifies the jsonpath to the replicas field for the scale's spec.

fields.name: statuspath
fields.summary: specifies the jsonpath to the replicas field for the scale's status.

markers.name: kubebuilder:subresource:status
markers.summary: enables the "/status" subresource on a CRD.

markers.name: kubebuilder:unservedversion
markers.summary: does not serve this version.
markers.details: This is useful if you need to drop support for a version in favor of a newer version.

markers.name: versionName
markers.summary: overrides the API group version for this package (defaults to the package name).

markers.name: kubebuilder:pruning:PreserveUnknownFields
markers.summary: PreserveUnknownFields stops the apiserver from pruning fields which are not specified.
markers.details:
By default the apiserver drops unknown fields from the request payload
during the decoding step. This marker stops the API server from doing so.
It affects fields recursively, but switches back to normal pruning behaviour
if nested  properties or additionalProperties are specified in the schema.
This can either be true or undefined. False
is forbidden.

NB: The kubebuilder:validation:XPreserveUnknownFields variant is deprecated
in favor of the kubebuilder:pruning:PreserveUnknownFields variant.  They function
identically.

markers.details:

must be used. It can only be used when ListType is set to map, and the keys
should be scalar types.

markers.name: listType
markers.summary: specifies the type of data-structure that the list
markers.details:
represents (map, set, atomic).

Possible data-structure types of a list are:

  - "map": it needs to have a key field, which will be used to build an
    associative list. A typical example is a the pod container list,
    which is indexed by the container name.

  - "set": Fields need to be "scalar", and there can be only one
    occurrence of each.

  - "atomic": All the fields in the list are treated as a single value,
    are typically manipulated together by the same actor.

markers.name: mapType
markers.summary: specifies the level of atomicity of the map;
markers.details:
i.e. whether each item in the map is independent of the others,
or all fields are treated as a single unit.

Possible values:

  - "granular": items in the map are independent of each other,
    and can be manipulated by different actors.
    This is the default behavior.

  - "atomic": all fields are treated as one unit.
    Any changes have to replace the entire map.

markers.name: default
markers.summary: Default sets the default value for this field.
markers.details:
A default value will be accepted as any value valid for the field.
Only JSON-formatted values are accepted. `ref(...)` values are ignored.
Formatting for common types include: boolean: `true`, string:
`"Cluster"`, numerical: `1.24`, array: `[1,2]`, object: `{"policy":
"delete"}`). Defaults should be defined in pruned form, and only best-effort
validation will be performed. Full validation of a default requires
submission of the containing CRD to an apiserver.

fields.name: namespace

fields.details:
If not set, the Rule belongs to the generated ClusterRole.
If set, the Rule belongs to a Role, whose namespace is specified by this field.

fields.details:
Create requests cannot be restricted by resourcename, as the object's name
is not known at authorization time.

markers.name: kubebuilder:webhook
markers.summary: specifies how a webhook should be served.
markers.details:
It specifies only the details that are intrinsic to the application serving
it (e.g. the resources it can handle, or the path it serves on).

fields.name: admissionReviewVersions
fields.summary: is an ordered list of preferred `AdmissionReview`
fields.details: versions the Webhook expects.

fields.name: failurePolicy
fields.summary: specifies what should happen if the API server cannot reach the webhook.
fields.details:
It may be either "ignore" (to skip the webhook and continue on) or "fail" (to reject
the object in question).

fields.name: groups
fields.summary: specifies the API groups that this webhook receives requests for.

fields.name: matchPolicy
fields.summary: defines how the "rules" list is used to match incoming requests.
fields.details:
Allowed values are "Exact" (match only if it exactly matches the specified rule)
or "Equivalent" (match a request if it modifies a resource listed in rules, even via another API group or version).

fields.name: mutating
fields.summary: marks this as a mutating webhook (it's validating only if false)
fields.details:
Mutating webhooks are allowed to change the object in their response,
and are called *before* all validating webhooks.  Mutating webhooks may
choose to reject an object, similarly to a validating webhook.

fields.name: name
fields.summary: indicates the name of this webhook configuration. Should be a domain with at least three segments separated by dots

fields.name: path
fields.summary: specifies that path that the API server should connect to this webhook on. Must be
fields.details:
prefixed with a '/validate-' or '/mutate-' depending on the type, and followed by
$GROUP-$VERSION-$KIND where all values are lower-cased and the periods in the group
are substituted for hyphens. For example, a validating webhook path for type
batch.tutorial.kubebuilder.io/v1,Kind=CronJob would be
/validate-batch-tutorial-kubebuilder-io-v1-cronjob

fields.name: reinvocationPolicy
fields.summary: allows mutating webhooks to request reinvocation after other mutations
fields.details:
To allow mutating admission plugins to observe changes made by other plugins,
built-in mutating admission plugins are re-run if a mutating webhook modifies
an object, and mutating webhooks can specify a reinvocationPolicy to control
whether they are reinvoked as well.

fields.name: resources
fields.summary: specifies the API resources that this webhook receives requests for.

fields.name: serviceName
fields.summary: indicates the name of the K8s Service the webhook uses.

fields.name: serviceNamespace
fields.summary: indicates the namespace of the K8s Service the webhook uses.

fields.name: servicePort
fields.summary: indicates the port of the K8s Service the webhook uses

fields.name: sideEffects
fields.summary: specify whether calling the webhook will have side effects.
fields.details:
This has an impact on dry runs and `kubectl diff`: if the sideEffect is "Unknown" (the default) or "Some", then
the API server will not call the webhook on a dry-run request and fails instead.
If the value is "None", then the webhook has no side effects and the API server will call it on dry-run.
If the value is "NoneOnDryRun", then the webhook is responsible for inspecting the "dryRun" property of the
AdmissionReview sent in the request, and avoiding side effects if that value is "true."

fields.name: timeoutSeconds
fields.summary: allows configuring how long the API server should wait for a webhook to respond before treating the call as a failure.
fields.details:
If the timeout expires before the webhook responds, the webhook call will be ignored or the API call will be rejected based on the failure policy.
The timeout value must be between 1 and 30 seconds.
The timeout for an admission webhook defaults to 10 seconds.

fields.name: url
fields.summary: allows mutating webhooks configuration to specify an external URL when generating
fields.details:
the manifests, instead of using the internal service communication. Should be in format of
https://address:port/path
When this option is specified, the serviceConfig.Service is removed from webhook the manifest.
The URL configuration should be between quotes.
`url` cannot be specified when `path` is specified.

fields.name: verbs
fields.summary: specifies the Kubernetes API verbs that this webhook receives requests for.
fields.details:
Only modification-like verbs may be specified.
May be "create", "update", "delete", "connect", or "*" (for all).

fields.name: versions
fields.summary: specifies the API versions that this webhook receives requests for.

fields.name: webhookVersions
fields.summary: specifies the target API versions of the {Mutating,Validating}WebhookConfiguration objects
fields.details: itself to generate. The only supported value is v1. Defaults to v1.
